tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

package com.example.ancapp

import android.content.ContentValues
import android.content.Context
import android.database.Cursor
import android.database.sqlite.SQLiteDatabase
import android.database.sqlite.SQLiteOpenHelper
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.Period
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit

enum class DangerSign(val label: String) {
  VAGINAL_BLEEDING("Vaginal bleeding"),
  SEVERE_HEADACHE("Severe headache"),
  BLURRED_VISION("Blurred vision"),
  FEVER("Fever"),
}

data class Patient(val id: Long, val name: String, val dob: LocalDate, val dueDate: LocalDate) {
  fun ageOn(day: LocalDate): Int = Period.between(dob, day).years
  fun gestationalWeeksOn(day: LocalDate): Int = gestationalWeeks(dueDate, day)
}

// Naegele's rule: LMP is 280 days before the due date.
fun gestationalWeeks(dueDate: LocalDate, on: LocalDate): Int =
  (ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(dueDate.minusDays(280), on) / 7).toInt()

data class Visit(
  val id: Long = 0,
  val patientId: Long,
  val date: LocalDate,
  val gestationWeeks: Int,
  val weightKg: Double,
  val systolic: Int,
  val diastolic: Int,
  val hemoglobin: Double?,
  val dangerSigns: Set<DangerSign>,
  val notes: String,
)

// ponytail: plain SQLiteOpenHelper, no Room/KSP. Add Room if the schema grows.
class AncDatabase(context: Context) : SQLiteOpenHelper(context, "anc.db", null, 1) {

  override fun onCreate(db: SQLiteDatabase) {
    db.execSQL("CREATE TABLE patient (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, dob TEXT NOT NULL, due_date TEXT NOT NULL)")
    db.execSQL(
      """CREATE TABLE visit (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        patient_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES patient(id),
        visit_date TEXT NOT NULL,
        gestation_weeks INTEGER NOT NULL,
        weight_kg REAL NOT NULL,
        systolic INTEGER NOT NULL,
        diastolic INTEGER NOT NULL,
        hemoglobin REAL,
        danger_signs TEXT NOT NULL,
        notes TEXT NOT NULL
      )"""
    )
    // Starting data from clinic records.
    seed(db, "Emily Carter", "1996-04-12", "2026-12-05", "2026-08-10", 68.5, 118, 76, 11.8)
    seed(db, "Sarah Mitchell", "1990-11-02", "2027-01-20", "2026-08-12", 61.2, 110, 70, 12.4)
    seed(db, "Grace Thompson", "2001-07-30", "2026-10-15", "2026-08-05", 72.0, 128, 84, 10.2)
  }

  override fun onUpgrade(db: SQLiteDatabase, oldVersion: Int, newVersion: Int) {
    // Only version 1 exists.
  }

  fun pregnantPatients(today: LocalDate): List<Patient> =
    readableDatabase.rawQuery(
      "SELECT id, name, dob, due_date FROM patient WHERE due_date >= ? ORDER BY due_date",
      arrayOf(today.toString()),
    ).use { c -> buildList { while (c.moveToNext()) add(c.toPatient()) } }

  fun visits(patientId: Long): List<Visit> =
    readableDatabase.rawQuery(
      "SELECT id, patient_id, visit_date, gestation_weeks, weight_kg, systolic, diastolic, hemoglobin, danger_signs, notes " +
        "FROM visit WHERE patient_id = ? ORDER BY visit_date DESC, id DESC",
      arrayOf(patientId.toString()),
    ).use { c -> buildList { while (c.moveToNext()) add(c.toVisit()) } }

  fun addVisit(visit: Visit): Long = writableDatabase.insertVisit(visit)

  private fun seed(
    db: SQLiteDatabase,
    name: String,
    dob: String,
    due: String,
    visitDate: String,
    weight: Double,
    systolic: Int,
    diastolic: Int,
    hemoglobin: Double,
  ) {
    val patientId = db.insert("patient", null, ContentValues().apply {
      put("name", name)
      put("dob", dob)
      put("due_date", due)
    })
    val date = LocalDate.parse(visitDate)
    db.insertVisit(
      Visit(
        patientId = patientId,
        date = date,
        gestationWeeks = gestationalWeeks(LocalDate.parse(due), date),
        weightKg = weight,
        systolic = systolic,
        diastolic = diastolic,
        hemoglobin = hemoglobin,
        dangerSigns = emptySet(),
        notes = "Imported from clinic records.",
      )
    )
  }

  private fun SQLiteDatabase.insertVisit(v: Visit): Long = insert("visit", null, ContentValues().apply {
    put("patient_id", v.patientId)
    put("visit_date", v.date.toString())
    put("gestation_weeks", v.gestationWeeks)
    put("weight_kg", v.weightKg)
    put("systolic", v.systolic)
    put("diastolic", v.diastolic)
    put("hemoglobin", v.hemoglobin)
    put("danger_signs", v.dangerSigns.joinToString(",") { it.name })
    put("notes", v.notes)
  })

  private fun Cursor.toPatient() = Patient(
    id = getLong(0),
    name = getString(1),
    dob = LocalDate.parse(getString(2)),
    dueDate = LocalDate.parse(getString(3)),
  )

  private fun Cursor.toVisit() = Visit(
    id = getLong(0),
    patientId = getLong(1),
    date = LocalDate.parse(getString(2)),
    gestationWeeks = getInt(3),
    weightKg = getDouble(4),
    systolic = getInt(5),
    diastolic = getInt(6),
    hemoglobin = if (isNull(7)) null else getDouble(7),
    dangerSigns = getString(8).split(",").filter { it.isNotEmpty() }.map { DangerSign.valueOf(it) }.toSet(),
    notes = getString(9),
  )
}

content.text:
The app builds, runs on the emulator, and the ANC visit flow works end to end, including after a force-stop and relaunch.

**What's in place** (three files under `app/src/main/java/com/example/ancapp/`):
- **`Data.kt`**: models, plus a SQLite database created with the platform `SQLiteOpenHelper`. It seeds the three clinic patients and their prior visits on first creation. Gestational age is derived from the due date (LMP = due − 280 days).
- **`AncViewModel.kt`**: holds the current screen and loads and saves data off the main thread.
- **`MainActivity.kt`**: the three Compose screens.
  - **Register:** patients with `due_date` on or after today, sorted by due date, showing name, age, due date, and weeks.
  - **Detail:** the patient's visits, newest first, with date, weeks, weight, BP, Hb if recorded, danger signs, and notes.
  - **New visit form:** date, gestational age (prefilled from the due date), weight, systolic/diastolic, danger signs (None plus four options), and notes. Save stays disabled until required fields are valid.

**Verification:**
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds after one fix (an internal Compose import).
- Installed on `emulator-5554` and launched. The register screen shows Grace, Emily, and Sarah, sorted by due date.
- Opened Emily's detail screen and saved a new visit (2026-10-13, 70.2 kg, 120/80). It appeared in the list.
- Force-stopped and relaunched the app. The new visit was still there.
- Logcat for the app's pid shows no errors or crashes. The `E` lines I saw earlier came from Google Play services and the system, not the app.

**Choices and gaps:**
- Hemoglobin is not on the form, since the spec didn't list it. Seeded Hb values show in the detail view.
- Danger signs: I only tested None in the UI. The multi-select logic is written but not exercised on the device.
- No unit tests were added.
- I left the existing `applicationId` (`com.example.ancapp.builda`) unchanged.
- The emulator's database now contains one test visit I added for Emily. Uninstall the app to clear it.
- I did not commit anything.
